Sea Stock Tumbles: What's Going On?
sum: Sea Ltd SE shares are moving lower Tuesday. The company introduced Sea Cloud, an AI-focused enterprise platform that marks its entry into a new business segment. Here’s what you should know.
Sea Turns Proprietary Cloud Infrastructure Into Commercial Offering

The company revealed the initiative in an employee anniversary letter filed with the SEC through Form 6-K, celebrating nine years since its New York Stock Exchange listing. Sea said it has spent more than a decade developing and operating its own cloud infrastructure, which currently powers Garena, Shopee and Monee 24 hours a day.

Over the last two years, about 500 employees have reengineered the platform to handle AI workloads. According to Sea, the upgrades have significantly reduced the time required to take AI projects from development to production. The company now intends to offer the service to external customers under the Sea Cloud name.

Management likened the move to Shopee’s early decision to focus on mobile commerce while competitors remained centered on desktop platforms. Sea believes its long experience running infrastructure for large-scale consumer businesses gives it an advantage that rivals cannot easily replicate.

The letter also pointed to the possibility of a major corporate restructuring. Sea said Monee is approaching a stage where it could function as a standalone business, and suggested that a public listing could provide additional capital and greater flexibility for future growth. The company added that it could potentially ring the NYSE opening bell once again.

Sea also highlighted the expansion of its businesses since going public. Garena’s quarterly active user base increased from 69 million to 666 million, Shopee’s quarterly gross merchandise value grew from $1.1 billion to $38.3 billion, and quarterly revenue climbed from $94 million to $7.8 billion.

items.t: Sea Ltd Stock (SE) Closed Down by 5.55% on Sep 15: A Full Analysis
sum: Sea Ltd (SE) closed down by 5.55%. The Software & IT Services sector is down by 1.05%. The company underperformed the industry. Top 3 stocks by turnover in the sector: Meta Platforms Inc (META) up 0.70%; Oracle Corp (ORCL) down 3.07%; Microsoft Corp (MSFT) down 1.68%.

Sea Limited experienced significant downward price momentum during today's trading session, largely driven by a concentration of high-profile insider share sales and negative sentiment surrounding recent executive disclosures. Filings with the Securities and Exchange Commission revealed that several top executives, including the Chief Operating Officer, the Chief Corporate Officer, and key board directors, executed multiple open-market share sales under Rule 10b5-1 trading plans. The persistent pattern of insider liquidations in recent days raised caution among institutional and retail market participants, triggering profit-taking and accelerating short-term selling pressure.

Compounding the pressure from insider transactions, the market continues to absorb the implications of the company's latest quarterly financial results. Although Sea Limited demonstrated solid top-line growth driven by expansion in its e-commerce platform and digital financial services, its bottom-line earnings per share missed consensus expectations by a noticeable margin. This profitability shortfall has prompted analysts at major brokerage firms to revise their near-term earnings estimates lower, eroding investor sentiment and overshadowing the company's robust revenue trajectory.

Broader market dynamics and macroeconomic positioning also contributed to today's sell-off. Market sentiment across technology and emerging market growth equities remained cautious as investors adjusted positions ahead of key inflation data releases and upcoming central bank policy decisions. Additionally, investor positioning shifted into a defensive stance ahead of the company's scheduled annual general meeting. The combination of executive share liquidations, earnings estimate downgrades, and macroeconomic uncertainty created strong headwinds for the stock during the session.
Technically, Sea Ltd (SE) shows a MACD (12,26,9) value of -3.369, indicating a sell signal.

sum: ASEAN’s digital economy is shifting from user growth towards deeper monetisation, with Grab and Sea increasingly using payments, lending and other financial services to strengthen their ecosystems. We look at what their Q2 2026 results reveal about this shift, and how Singapore investors can access both stocks through the new Grab and Sea SDRs on SGX.
Grab and Sea reported continued growth in financial services alongside their core mobility, delivery and e-commerce businesses.
But the latest results from Grab and Sea suggest the next phase of growth may look different.
Instead of simply adding more users, both companies are increasingly focused on deepening relationships with existing users through financial services.
This includes payments, lending and, in Grab’s case, digital banking and wealth management.
These services can make the platforms more useful to consumers and merchants, while also creating new revenue streams beyond mobility, delivery and e-commerce.
In this report, we look at what Grab and Sea’s Q2 2026 results tell us about this shift in ASEAN fintech.

Tiger Global Portfolio: Chase Coleman’s Top Holdings (2026)
sum: Founded by Chase Coleman, one of Julian Robertson’s best-known “Tiger Cubs,” Tiger Global Management has become a leading crossover investment firm. It combines public equity investing with private venture capital under a single investment platform.

This article breaks down the Tiger Global portfolio, delivering a comprehensive analysis of its current 2026 13F long book and highlighting Coleman’s top high-conviction technology and growth holdings. Beyond the public stock portfolio, we explore Tiger Global‘s origins and investment philosophy. The firm’s crossover strategy combines aggressive investing across both public and private markets.

Source: Tiger Global Management LLC Form 13F-HR for Q1 2026 (as of March 31, 2026), filed with the SEC on May 15, 2026 (EDGAR, CIK 0001167483). Reflects US-listed long positions only, not the firm’s private/venture holdings or total AUM.
As of its Q1 2026 filing, Tiger Global reported ~$22.85 billion in US-listed long positions across 54 holdings, a ~23% decline in portfolio value from the prior quarter.

The position count held steady at 54, but that stability is deceptive. Tiger Global exited seven holdings outright, including Flutter Entertainment, Veeva Systems and Grab, together worth roughly $2.3 billion at the end of 2025, and replaced them with seven new ones. The remainder of the ~$6.9 billion decline came from trimming existing stakes and from falling prices, as the Q1 2026 drawdown in growth and semiconductor names weighed on the book.

The portfolio is highly concentrated: its five largest positions account for roughly 48% of the 13F book. These positions are largely centered on mega-cap technology companies and semiconductor leaders, including Alphabet, NVIDIA, Amazon, and TSMC. This reflects Tiger Global’s strong conviction that AI, cloud computing, and semiconductor infrastructure will continue to drive long-term growth.

Beyond its largest holdings, the portfolio remains focused on technology and digital innovation. Tiger Global maintains significant investments in semiconductor equipment through Applied Materials and in fintech companies such as Corpay, Chime, Nu Holdings, Wealthfront, and Block.

items.t: Indonesia asks four e-commerce platforms to collect income tax from sellers
sum: From Aug 1, the platforms must collect and pass on income tax on sales made by small- and medium-sized sellers

[JAKARTA] Indonesia’s tax office said on Wednesday (Jul 1) it has asked e-commerce marketplaces Tokopedia, Shopee, Lazada and Blibli to collect income taxes from sellers based on sales made on their platforms, with the policy to take effect from August.

The tax office said it has appointed Tokopedia – which is controlled by ByteDance’s TikTok and also partly owned by Indonesia’s biggest tech company GoTo Group – Sea’s Shopee, the Alibaba-backed Lazada and Blibli as platforms that must become tax collectors.
Sellers with turnover of 500 million rupiah (US$28,000) or less will be exempted from having taxes collected if they provide a letter to the tax office, according to the statement.
The finance ministry in 2025 issued a regulation requiring e-commerce platforms that meet certain criteria to collect and pass on income tax on sales made by small- and medium-sized sellers.
The regulation also requires these platforms to pass on information regarding sales to tax authorities.
After complaints from sellers and platforms, the policy was postponed to 2026.
